business_problem: Woolworths needed to replace tightly coupled legacy e-commerce systems that produced stale batch data, slowed releases, and made it expensive to scale fast-growing inventory, fulfillment, and promotions workloads.
solution_summary: Woolworths adopted MongoDB Atlas as the data platform behind a modular, API-centric retail architecture so it could scale critical e-commerce services independently instead of scaling whole monolithic systems. Atlas now powers loyalty, fulfillment, supply chain, and digital payments services that were replatformed from rigid relational designs to a flexible document model. Real-time stock-on-hand updates replaced batch inventory cycles, promotional rules and pricing offers are stored centrally so the same logic can be applied consistently across digital channels, and fulfillment services allocate orders dynamically across Woolworths' own fleet and partners such as Uber and DoorDash. Because MongoDB Atlas supports fast feature delivery without downtime, Woolworths can add capabilities quickly while preserving resilience and preparing a group-wide product catalogue for future AI-driven e-commerce experiences.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs Woolworths' modular e-commerce services for inventory, fulfillment, promotions, loyalty, supply chain, and payments.

data_flow: Inventory, pricing, promotion, and fulfillment events are stored in MongoDB Atlas and served through API-centric services that update stock in near real time, apply basket pricing consistently across channels, and route delivery orders dynamically to Woolworths' fleet or courier partners.
business_outcome: Woolworths improved product availability, faster delivery, and promotional consistency for millions of shoppers while sustaining rapid digital growth on a resilient platform.
metrics: Woolworths Group has over 200,000 employees, over 1,500 stores, and revenues of more than $67 billion Australian dollars.
Between 2020 and 2025, the company's online business grew from AU$2 billion to AU$8 billion.
WooliesX fulfilled 44.1 million e-commerce orders during the 2025 financial period.
Over 55% of online customer orders are fulfilled on the same day, with 41% in less than two hours.
With MongoDB Atlas, 90% of the updates are completed in less than 60 seconds.
MongoDB provided four years continuous uptime.
architecture_clues: Atlas has powered Woolworths' modern architecture since 2019.
The platform uses modular, decoupled API-centric services that can be scaled independently.
Promotional rules and pricing logic are centralized so all digital channels consume the same data source.
evidence_quotes: We knew that with the kind of growth we were experiencing, we needed a modern and flexible data platform.
We selected MongoDB Atlas due to its high performance, predictability, and flexibility.
MongoDB was consistently able to adapt to our rapid pace of growth, allowing us to release features faster, without any downtime.
Orders are now dynamically allocated to the delivery fleet or courier partners in real time.
